conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: CONSTANT RECORD clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: "The CONSTANT RECORD clause may be specified only in the local-storage or working-storage sections." (cite.py --check 13.18.15.3 OK). DataBinder errors COBOLNET1549 when item.IsConstantRecord && section is not WorkingStorage/LocalStorage. Probes (pinned cobol.exe, --std 2023): FILE SECTION record -> COBOLNET1549 SR1; LINKAGE SECTION -> COBOLNET1549 SR1; LOCAL-STORAGE -> accepted, runs `[LSOK00]`; WORKING-STORAGE accepted. SCREEN SECTION and REPORT SECTION entries are rejected too, but at parse (COBOLNET0901 'CONSTANT' is a reserved word) rather than by the SR1 diagnostic - rejected as required, less precise message. Communication section not probed. No negative fixture pins SR1 (existing constant-record-* negatives cover level / 85 gate / stores / SR13 only) -> test-needed. || Code sites (adjudicator detail): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs#BindEntries (section check at the IsConstantRecord placement arm, COBOLNET1549)
rows.rule-text: The CONSTANT RECORD clause may be specified only in the local-storage or working-storage sections.

rows.subject: CONTROL clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 13.18.16.4 "Data-name-1 shall not reference a zero-length group item" -> OK 6). Zero-length group per §8.5.4 (cite.py --check 8.5.4 "A group data item containing only an occurs-depending table in which the number of occurrences is zero" -> OK 1)): item 1 (group of only an ODO table) and item 2 (group of only a zero-length subordinate, recursively ODO or DYNAMIC LENGTH) are always rejected at bind by ControlOperandShapeViolation's SR5 arm (OdoModel.TableUnder, cite OK §13.18.16.3 5)) and SR7 arm (HasVariableLengthSubordinate, cite OK §13.18.16.3 7)); items 3/4 are elementary, not groups; item 5 (a variable-length logical record whose runtime length is zero) is a run-time state the GR constrains the PROGRAM against with no exception condition or specified outcome, so no implementation action is required. Existing negatives pb177-control-occurs-depending / pb177-control-variable-length-group are SR5/SR7 witnesses whose groups have nonzero minimum length, so they do not witness GR6 as such; test-ref empty. || Editions (adjudicator): 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (text as in 2023; Annex E carries no edition note for it)
rows.rule-text: Data-name-1 shall not reference a zero-length group item.

rows.subject: COPY statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR4: 'If the SUPPRESS phrase is specified, library text incorporated as a result of COPY statement processing is not listed. If a listing is being produced, the COPY statement itself is listed.' cite.py --check 7.2.3.4 'If the SUPPRESS phrase is specified, library text incorporated as a result of COPY statement processing is not listed' -> OK §7.2.3.4 4). COBOL.NET produces no source listing (docs/CONFORMANCE.md: '>>LISTING / >>PAGE ... no source listing is produced'; A.1 item 200 is conditioned on the implementor producing listings), so both halves hold vacuously; SUPPRESS [PRINTING] is accepted (ResolveOneCopy scans past it to the period) — probe p2c (COPY p2book SUPPRESS.) incorporated the text. ⚠ The SUPPRESS phrase is NOT harmless: because it is skipped by the scan-to-period rather than parsed, a REPLACING phrase that follows it (the general-format order) is silently discarded — filed against GR8/GR6 (finding 'COPY phrase parse is positional'). The legacy integration test SourceTextSpecTests.CopySuppressPrinting_IsBenignAndStillCopies exercises CobolSharp.Compiler, not Cobol.Net, so it does not close this row. probe dir E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec/scratchpad/adj-d2/out/probe/copy-p2/ || editions (adjudicator): 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (COPY statement present in every edition; Annex E.2 item 1 bullet 4 touches only non-pseudo-text REPLACING operands at 2023)
rows.rule-text: If the SUPPRESS phrase is specified, library text incorporated as a result of COPY statement processing is not listed. If a listing is being produced, the COPY statement itself is listed.

rows.subject: COPY statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR5: 'At the completion of copying the library text into the compilation group, the LISTING directive that is in effect for the COPY statement itself is considered to be in effect, regardless of any LISTING directives in the library text.' No source listing is produced (docs/CONFORMANCE.md §5 prose: '>>LISTING / >>PAGE (§7.3.18 / §7.3.19) — no source listing is produced, so listing on/off and page ejects are inert'); the LISTING directive is recognized and consumed, carrying no state that could leak out of a copybook. Vacuously satisfied; no observable behaviour to test. || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the LISTING directive is a §7.3 compiler directive; the rule is moot at 85, which has no directives)
rows.rule-text: At the completion of copying the library text into the compilation group, the LISTING directive that is in effect for the COPY statement itself is considered to be in effect, regardless of any LISTING directives in the library text.

rows.subject: COPY statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR11: 'The resultant text after replacement shall be in logical free-form reference format. When copying text-words into the resultant text, additional spaces may be introduced only between text-words where there already exists a space or at the end of a source line.' Library text is converted to free form (NormalizeCopybookMapped -> ConvertFixedToFreeMapped / NormalizeToFreeFormMapped) before replacement; ApplyReplacements copies unmatched spans verbatim (AppendSlice) and inserts pseudo-text-2 in place of the matched span with no added space; a partial-word match concatenates replacement and remainder with no space (probe p10: LEADING ==PFX-== BY ==NEW-== produced NEW-NAME-SFX, referenced successfully). No spec-derived test pins the spacing. || editions (adjudicator): 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (COPY statement present in every edition; Annex E.2 item 1 bullet 4 touches only non-pseudo-text REPLACING operands at 2023)
rows.rule-text: The resultant text after replacement shall be in logical free-form reference format. When copying text-words into the resultant text, additional spaces may be introduced only between text-words where there already exists a space or at the end of a source line.

rows.subject: Character sets
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: "The number of bytes used in the memory of the computer to represent characters in the national coded character set shall be the same for all characters in that coded character set; the number of bytes shall be determined at compile time." (cite.py --check 8.1.2 -> OK §8.1.2 2)). National = one UTF-16 code unit per position, BytesPerNational = 2 (a compile-time const, D-N1); every code unit U+0000-U+FFFF has a total 2-byte UTF-16BE image (PutNat/NatReadWindow are exact inverses for national content). NOTE 3 ("COBOL processes each fixed-size element of a character set as one character", --check OK) edge probed - cs1/p3.cob: LENGTH(N"😀€")=3 BYTE-LENGTH=6 (the surrogate pair is two positions), PIC N(4) BYTE-LENGTH 8; N"€A" in a PIC N(2) redefined as X(4) reads bytes 0x20 0xAC 0x00 0x41 (ORD 33 173 1 66) - uniform, lossless. No spec-derived test pins this rule; test-needed. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2002, 2014, 2023 (national class introduced in ISO/IEC 1989:2002)
rows.rule-text: The number of bytes used in the memory of the computer to represent characters in the national coded character set shall be the same for all characters in that coded character set; the number of bytes shall be determined at compile time.

rows.subject: Class and category of data items and literals
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 8.5.2.12 OK 1)): 'An elementary data item described as numeric by its PICTURE character-string and not described with a BLANK WHEN ZERO clause.' PictureAnalyzer.Analyze returns PicCategory.Numeric from its fall-through arm only when no editing symbol is present AND NOT (blankWhenZero && digits>0 && !signed && usage display/national) — the BWZ arm returns NumericEdited (line ~429). A signed or non-display BWZ subject is refused by §13.18.8.3 SR1/SR2 (DataBinder.BlankWhenZeroViolation, CheckClauseSubjects), so no numeric-PICTURE+BWZ item survives as category numeric. Probes (2023, probe/cc2): p1.cob plain PIC 9(3) accepted by SET CONTENT OF N1 TO FARTHEST-FROM-ZERO (-> 999, §14.9.39.3 SR31 'numeric data item') ; n1/n3/n4/n7 — PIC 9(3) BLANK WHEN ZERO and PIC 9(3)V9 BLANK WHEN ZERO are REFUSED as numeric data items (COBOLNET1938 SR31, COBOLNET0844 §8.8.1.1, COBOLNET2216 §8.8.4.4.3 SR6); g85b.cob same at --std 85. Both halves verified. No single spec-derived test pins BOTH halves (Strict_AcceptsNumericOperands pins the numeric half only; the BWZ-exclusion half as a numeric-operand refusal has no golden), so test-ref left empty = test-needed. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (numeric PICTURE category and the BLANK WHEN ZERO exclusion are in every edition)
rows.rule-text: An elementary data item described as numeric by its PICTURE character-string and not described with a BLANK WHEN ZERO clause.

rows.subject: Class and category of data items and literals
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: '1) An elementary data item explicitly or implicitly described as usage index.' (cite.py OK). Both halves probed at --std 85 and 2023 (p5.cob/p6.cob): '01 G USAGE INDEX. 05 I1. 05 I2.' -- the IMPLICIT (inherited) leaves are index data items: SET I1 TO TX / SET TX TO I1 round-trip (TE(TX)=D), I1 < I2 relation true, MOVE 5 TO I1 rejected COBOLNET0809 (§14.9.25.3 SR1 class index) and COMPUTE N = I1 + 1 rejected COBOLNET0844 (class index not numeric). Explicit form covered by many goldens (e.g. 85/pb212_operand_class_screens) but no spec-derived test pins the IMPLICIT (group-inherited) half, so test-ref left empty (test-needed). [code-location note: (Usage.Index -> PicInfo.IndexItem)]
rows.rule-text: An elementary data item explicitly or implicitly described as usage index.

rows.subject: Common phrases and features for statements
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule 3 (--check 14.7.6 -> OK §14.7.6 3)): CorrMatch admits an ADD/SUBTRACT pair only when both Pic.Category are Numeric. PROBE c2.cob ADD CORRESPONDING G1 TO G2: BINARY-LONG 3+10=13, FLOAT-LONG 2.5+10=12.5, COMP-2 1.5+10=11.5 all pair (numeric data items); a numeric-EDITED namesake NE (ZZ9) is not paired (stays ' 10'); a group SG descends and pairs its numeric children (12). l1_subtract_corr_word_equivalence pins only the positive pairing, no golden pins the non-numeric exclusion - test-needed. || editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023
rows.rule-text: In an ADD or SUBTRACT statement, both of the data items are numeric data items.

rows.subject: Common phrases and features for statements
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule 5 (--check 14.7.6 -> OK §14.7.6 5)). The recursion descends only through CorrEligible groups, so nothing under a subordinate OCCURS/REDEFINES group is reached; for a THROUGH-alias operand CorrMembers walks each included item's ancestors up to the window's enclosing group (PB966). PROBE c2.cob: O1 under 'OG OCCURS 1' in D1 is not paired with O1 under a plain OG in D2 (OG of G2 stays 0); out/probe/corr/c3.cob: FF under 'FILLER REDEFINES FF' is not reached. D1 itself with a REDEFINES clause is correctly NOT excluded (c1.cob S4: ADD CORRESPONDING M1R TO M2 where M1R REDEFINES M1 pairs KK). No golden isolates rule 5 - test-needed. || editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023
rows.rule-text: Neither data item is subordinate to a group item that is subordinate to D1 or D2 when the group item contains an OCCURS or REDEFINES clause.

rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule 1 (--check 14.7.7 -> OK §14.7.7 1)): mixed descriptions need no user conversion. PROBE out/probe/arith/a1.cob (native): PIC 9(31) receiver with a NUMVAL function result, FLOAT-BINARY-64, BINARY-DOUBLE and a floating literal operand -> 13 (5 + 1 + 2 + 3 + 2, fractional 0.5 truncated at the store); a2.cob (STANDARD-DECIMAL): ADD S9(3)V9 + 9V99 GIVING Z9.99 ROUNDED -> 12.55, MULTIPLY ... GIVING 99 ROUNDED -> 01. The rule is exercised by essentially every arithmetic golden but no golden is written against it by name - test-ref left empty. || editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023
rows.rule-text: The data descriptions of the operands need not be the same; any necessary conversion and decimal point alignment is supplied throughout the calculation.

rows.subject: Common phrases and features for statements
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule 4 a)/b) + NOTE 3. PROBE out/probe/arith/a3.cob at 2023 and 85 (identical): ADD X TO X Y (X=5,Y=1) -> X=10 Y=6 (the intermediate 5 is fixed before the first store); COMPUTE X Y = X + 1 -> 6 6; MULTIPLY X BY X Y -> 25 10; SUBTRACT X FROM Y X -> Y=3 X=0; DIVIDE X INTO X Y -> 1 0; ADD 4 TO Z X Z -> Z stored twice left to right (9+4=13->3, then 3+4=7); receiver identification 'as each data item is accessed' (--check 14.7.7 -> OK, cite.py labels the b) paragraph '4) a)' - PB308 family): COMPUTE I T (I) = 2 -> T(2)=2, ADD 1 TO I T (I) -> T(2)=3; operand identification at start: ADD 1 T (I) TO I -> 2; NOTE 3 overlap: ADD GX TO GA where GX REDEFINES the group holding GA -> G=4634 (1246 truncated into GA, sender read once). Size error on one store leaves only that receiver unchanged (sizeerr/p1.cob E9/E10). PB654 (landed) removed the double evaluation on the PROHIBITED float arm. || REFUTED: CONFORMS (test-ref must be empty: pb157_compute_multi_sizeerr pins only 4 b)'s last sentence, not 4 a)'s intermediate-before-any-store, the left-to-right order or the item-identification timing) — The behaviour holds on every arm I attacked: FLOAT-LONG overlap (ADD FX TO FX FY -> 10 6; COMPUTE FX FY = FX * 2 -> 10 10; MULTIPLY FX BY FX FY -> 25 10), GIVING overlap (ADD X Y GIVING X Y -> 6 6), DIVIDE Y INTO X GIVING Y REMAINDER X (17/5 -> Y=3, X=2 from the original dividend), receiver identification after an earlier receiver changed its subscript (ADD 1 TO I GIVING I T (I) -> T(2); COMPUTE I T (I) ROUNDED = I + 1.5 -> I=2, T(2)=3), a REMAINDER target subscripted by the dividend. But the cited test-ref is a single-statement COMPUTE BIG SML = 123456 whose only assertion is 'SE / BIG=123456 SML=99' - the 4 b) size-error sentence. Nothing in it can fail if the intermediate were not fixed before the first store or receivers were identified at statement start. A test that pins one sentence of a multi-part rule cannot close the row. || editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023
rows.rule-text: The arithmetic statements may have single or multiple resultant identifiers. These statements have common rules for storing in the resultant identifiers. The execution of these statements proceeds in the following order: a) The initial evaluation of the statement is done and the result of this operation is placed in an intermediate data item. If any form of standard arithmetic is in effect, a standard intermediate data item of the form appropriate to that mode of arithmetic is used. Otherwise, an implementor-defined intermediate data item is used. The rules indicating which data items or literals are part of this evaluation are given in the rules for the individual statements. All item identification for the data items involved in the initial evaluation is done at the start of the execution of the statement. If the size error condition is raised during the initial evaluation, none of the resultant data items are changed and execution proceeds as indicated in 14.7.5, SIZE ERROR phrase and size error condition. b) If the size error condition was not raised during the initial evaluation, the intermediate data item is stored in or combined with and then stored in each single resulting data item in the left-to-right order in which the receiving data items are specified in the statement. Item identification for the receiving data items is done as each data item is accessed unless it was already done in step a. If the size error condition is raised when attempting to store in a resulting data item, only that data item remains unchanged and processing proceeds to the next resulting data item to the right. NOTE 3 Because rule 4 specifies the use of an intermediate data item to hold the value resulting from the initial arithmetic evaluation, and that arithmetic evaluation is complete before any data is moved from that intermediate data item to any receiving operands, the results contained in the receiving operands for all arithmetic statements are defined regardless of whether any of the sending operands share storage with any of the receiving operands. Those results in the receiving operands are the same as if no receiving operand shared any part of its storage area with any sending operand.
